messages.subject: [Basta-users] Individual Survival
messages.body_plain:
Hi BaSTA users,

I am a master student at Autonomous University of Madrid studying the  
effects of some individual variables on the survival of a rodent  
species. I am interested in getting both population survival and  
individual survival. I used MultiBasta function and I got that the  
model that best fits my database is Weibull-Bathtub.

Iâ€™m wondering if there is any function or another way to obtain the  
individual survival using BaSta from the estimated parameters. I could  
not find any information through the tutorials and code examples about  
getting individual survival.

Thanks,

Carlos Molinero

messages.body_plain:
Hi Carlos,

   Thank you for your interest on the package. I believe that, what you mean by individual survival you would like the estimated lifespans and their 95% credible intervals, isnâ€™t it?

   You can extract those as follows: say that you call your BaSTA output â€œoutâ€. Although it is a basta object, it works as a list. The estimated ages are in â€œout$agesQuantâ€, which is a 3 x ni matrix, where ni is the number of individuals with unknown times of birth and/or death. The columns are therefore the mean and lower and upper 95% credible intervals of the estimated ages at death.

Best,

  Fernando

messages.subject: [Basta-users] Individual Survival
messages.body_plain:
Hi Fernando,

Thank you very much for your response. Being able to obtain the  
lifespans with its credible intervals has been very useful for me  
since it was another objective of my research. However, what I meant  
in the question is the following: Basta estimates the population  
survival probability and mortality rate curves for males and females.  
I would like to know if it is possible to estimate the curve that each  
individual has and, therefore, the survival probability of each  
individual.

Thanks,

Carlos
